questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: couple produces rotation and translation? couple gives pure rotation
questions.question: A body is acted upon by two equal and opposite forces, that are NOT along the same straight line. The body will:

options.d: have both rectilinear and rotational motion

questions.solution: (b) have only rotational motion. The forces form a couple, which produces rotation only.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: moment of couple as vector quantity
questions.question: Which among the following is a vector quantity?
questions.solution: (d) moment of couple. Its direction is perpendicular to the plane of the two forces.

concepts: energy transformation in burning candle
questions.question: What is the correct energy transformation during burning of a candle?
questions.solution: (c) chemical → heat + light

concepts: frequency unchanged on refraction
questions.question: When a ray of light passes from one optical medium to another, which of the following physical quantities does NOT change?
questions.solution: (b) Frequency of the wave. Frequency depends on the source, not the medium.

concepts: EM spectrum wavelength order
questions.question: Which one of the following combinations is the correct ascending order of electromagnetic waves in terms of wavelength?
questions.solution: (a) Gamma-rays, visible light, microwaves

concepts: load-effort graph slope as mechanical advantage
questions.question: For a lever, a graph is plotted with load on Y-axis and effort on X-axis. Which of the following represents the slope of the graph?
questions.solution: (a) Mechanical advantage. Slope = load/effort = MA.

concepts: convex lens image size vs object position
questions.question: For a real image formed by a convex lens, the ratio of I : O = 2 : 5, then the object is: (I is the height of the image and O is the height of the object)
questions.solution: (b) beyond 2F. Image is smaller than the object only when the object is beyond 2F.

concepts: prism normal incidence, TIR, total deviation
questions.question: A ray of light is incident normally on a face of an equilateral prism. The ray gets totally reflected at the second refracting surface. The total deviation produced in the path of the ray is:
questions.solution: (b) 60°. Ray passes undeviated at AB, is totally reflected at AC (incidence 60°), then leaves BC normally; total deviation 30°+30° = 60°.

concepts: emf and terminal voltage V = E - Ir
questions.question: In a closed circuit containing a bulb and a cell, the electromotive force (ε) and the terminal voltage (V) is related as. (Given I is current and r is internal resistance.)
questions.solution: (b) V = ε – Ir, since ε = V + Ir.

concepts: specific heat capacity independent of mass
thermal capacity = m c
questions.question: A metal piece of mass 5 g has thermal capacity 2.5 JK−1. If the mass of the metal is tripled, then its specific heat capacity will be:
questions.solution: (d) 0.5 Jg−1K−1. c = 2.5/5 = 0.5 J g−1 K−1, unchanged by mass.

concepts: resonance air column pitch with water level
frequency vs length of air column
questions.question:
Assertion (A): As the level of water in a tall measuring cylinder kept under running tap rises, the pitch of sound gradually increases.
Reason (R): Frequency of sound is inversely proportional to the length of the water column.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (c) (A) is true but (R) is false. As water rises, the air column shortens and frequency increases; frequency is inversely proportional to the air column length, not the water column.

concepts: identifying series vs parallel in redrawn circuits
questions.question: In the given circuits Y and Z, the resistors, R1 and R2, are connected in:

options.c: parallel in Y and series in Z
options.d: series in Y and parallel in Z

questions.solution: (b) parallel in both the circuits. On redrawing, both resistors are across the same two points A and B in each circuit.
questions.figure_desc: Two circuit diagrams Y and Z, each with two resistors R1 and R2; both can be redrawn with R1 and R2 across the same pair of points (parallel).

concepts: alpha decay displacement law, atomic number decreases by 2

options.a: One group to the left of P
options.b: One group to the right of P
options.c: Two groups to the right of P
options.d: Two groups to the left of P

questions.solution: (d) Two groups to the left of P. Atomic number decreases by 2.

concepts: specific heat capacity and temperature rise from table
questions.question:
Each of the substances given below is supplied with same amount of heat. Which one will attain the highest temperature?
Specific heat capacity (cal/g°C): Lead 0.031; Aluminium 0.21; Copper 0.095; Iron 0.115
questions.solution: (d) Lead. The lowest specific heat capacity gives the highest temperature rise.

concepts: Lenz's law direction of induced current
questions.question: The following figure shows a small bar magnet falling freely through a copper ring. For the observer at A, the direction of the induced current will be:

options.a: clockwise when magnet is above and below the ring
options.b: anticlockwise when magnet is above and below the ring
options.c: anticlockwise when magnet is above the ring and clockwise when the magnet is below the ring
options.d: clockwise when magnet is above the ring and anticlockwise when the magnet is below the ring

questions.solution: (c) anticlockwise when magnet is above the ring and clockwise when the magnet is below the ring.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: centre of gravity of irregular lamina, suspended body equilibrium
questions.question:
A non-uniform kite is hanging freely from the branch of a tree as shown. Study the figure and answer the following:
(a) Fill in the blank. __________ (P, Q, R or S) is the most probable position of its centre of gravity.
(b) Support your answer to (a) with a reason.
questions.solution: (a) Q. (b) Drawing the medians, their meeting point is Q. For a uniform triangular lamina the meeting point of the medians is the centre of gravity; for the kite (a quadrilateral, split in triangles) Q is the most probable position of the centre of gravity.

marking_points.point: (b) reason: Q is the point where the medians meet / hanging body's CG lies vertically below the suspension point

questions.figure_desc: A kite-shaped body hanging from a branch, with four labelled points P, Q, R, S along its vertical axis; the kite hangs freely so its centre of gravity lies vertically below the suspension point.

concepts: time period from displacement-time graph
frequency vs tension of wire, pitch
questions.question:
The displacement–time graph of a sound wave produced by a vibrating wire is shown below. P, R, S, Q are marked on the graph; PR spans one complete wave (time period).
(a) How will you adjust the tension in the wire, to reduce the length of PR?
(b) Which characteristic of sound is affected by the reduction in the length of PR?
questions.solution: (a) PR is the time period. Reducing it means increasing frequency. Frequency is proportional to the square root of tension, so the tension must be increased. (b) Pitch (frequency).

marking_points.point: (a) Increase the tension (reducing time period increases frequency, f proportional to sqrt(T))

questions.figure_desc: Displacement vs time sine-like wave with points P, R on the time axis marking one full cycle (PR = time period) and Q, S as crest/trough points.

concepts: condition for TIR, rarer to denser
questions.question: A ray of light enters a rectangular glass slab submerged in water at an angle of incidence 55°. Does this ray undergo total internal reflection when it moves from water to glass? Justify your answer. (The critical angle for glass–water interface is 54°)
questions.solution: No. For total internal reflection the ray must travel from a denser to a rarer medium. Here it goes from water (rarer) to glass (denser), so there is no total internal reflection.

marking_points.point: No, it does not undergo TIR
Justification: light travels from rarer (water) to denser (glass) medium; TIR needs denser to rarer

According to the NEW colour convention which colour of wire is connected to:

questions.topic: Magnetised bar poles and field lines
concepts: solenoid polarity by current direction
magnetic field lines of bar magnet
questions.question:
Copper wire is wound around a steel bar FT. Current is allowed to pass through the coil for some time and then the bar is removed.
(a) Draw only the magnetised bar FT and mark its poles.
(b) Trace two magnetic lines of force around FT clearly indicating the direction.
questions.solution: (a) Bar FT with north pole at F and south pole at T (looking from the F side, the current was anticlockwise, so F end is north). (b) Two closed field lines drawn outside the magnet, leaving from the N pole (F), curving round and entering the S pole (T), with arrows pointing from N to S outside the magnet.

marking_points.point: (a) Bar drawn with correct poles: N at F, S at T
(b) Two field lines outside the magnet with arrows from N (F) to S (T)

questions.figure_desc: A steel bar FT with a copper coil wound on it carrying current; viewed from end F the current flows anticlockwise (so F becomes the north pole). Only the bar with ends F and T is shown.

A current flows through a metallic conductor for a long period of time. State the change you would expect in its:
(a) Resistance
(b) Resistivity
questions.solution: The conductor heats up and its temperature rises. (a) Resistance increases. (b) Resistivity increases.

concepts: alpha and beta decay on proton-neutron graph
mass number of daughter nucleus
questions.question:
Curium is a radioactive element with the symbol 247/96 Cm named in honour of Madam Curie. The graph of number of protons (Y-axis, 92 to 98) vs number of neutrons (X-axis, 146 to 154) for some elements is shown, with points P, Q, R, S.
(a) Which point on the graph indicates the element Cm?
(b) Which point on the graph indicates daughter nucleus after Cm undergoes radioactive decay of 1α followed by 2β?
(c) State the mass number of the daughter nucleus.
questions.solution: (a) P (96 protons, 247-96 = 151 neutrons). (b) After 1 alpha and 2 beta: atomic number 96-2+2 = 96, mass number 243, neutrons 243-96 = 147; this is point R. (c) 247 - 4 = 243.
questions.figure_desc: Graph of number of protons (92,94,96,98) vs number of neutrons (146 to 154) with four plotted points P, Q, R, S. From the solution P is at (151 neutrons, 96 protons) and R is at (147 neutrons, 96 protons); positions of Q and S are not stated.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: total internal reflection in prism, critical angle
ray tracing through prism
questions.question:
A prism has a 60° angle shown. Three rays I, J and H enter the prism as shown in the diagram.
(a) Out of the three rays (I, J, H) shown in the diagram, which ray will suffer Total Internal Reflection while inside the prism? (Critical angle of the prism is 42°.)
(b) Copy the diagram to complete the path of the ray which you have named in (a) till it comes out of the prism.
questions.solution: (a) Ray J. Inside the prism the angles of incidence of rays I, J, H are 30°, 60° and 30° respectively; only J (60°) exceeds the critical angle 42°. (b) Ray J is totally reflected at the face (angle of reflection 60°), travels on and meets the next face normally (0 degrees angle of incidence) and emerges undeviated.

marking_points.point: (a) Ray J, as its angle of incidence 60° exceeds the critical angle 42°
(b) J shown totally reflected at the prism face with angle of reflection equal to angle of incidence
(b) reflected ray shown emerging from the other face (normally, undeviated)

questions.figure_desc: An equilateral-type prism (60° angle marked) with three parallel/normally incident rays H, I and J entering the prism face; inside the prism the angles of incidence on the next face are 30° (I, H) and 60° (J).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: real and apparent depth
dispersion and refractive index with colour
apparent depth on inverting block
questions.question:
A rectangular glass block ABCD of refractive index 1.5 has an air bubble trapped inside it as shown in the diagram (the block is 15 cm across, between face AB and the opposite face). When seen from the surface AB, it appears to be 4 cm deep.
(a) Calculate the actual depth of the air bubble from the surface AB.
(b) For which colour of light, blue or yellow, the apparent depth will be greater?
(c) Turning the glass block upside down, DOES NOT change the apparent depth of the air bubble. State True or False.
questions.solution: (a) Refractive index = real depth / apparent depth, so real depth = 1.5 × 4 = 6 cm. (b) Yellow: it has a longer wavelength, hence smaller refractive index, hence greater apparent depth. (c) False: real depth from the new top face = 15 - 6 = 9 cm, apparent depth = 9/1.5 = 6 cm, which differs from 4 cm.

marking_points.point: (a) Formula μ = real depth/apparent depth with substitution
(b) Yellow, with reason (larger wavelength, smaller μ)

questions.figure_desc: Rectangular glass block ABCD with an air bubble inside; the dimension 15 cm is marked across the block (distance between face AB and the opposite face).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: ray diagram convex lens object at 2F
magnification independent of focal length? (image size depends on f)
questions.question:
(a) An object is placed at 2F position of a convex lens. Draw a ray diagram showing the formation of the image.
(b) How will the size of the image change if we, ONLY replace the lens in the above arrangement with another lens of a greater focal length?
questions.solution: (a) Object AB at 2F1: one ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through F2; another ray through the optical centre goes undeviated; they meet at 2F2 on the other side, forming a real, inverted image A'B' of the same size as the object. (b) The size of the image remains unchanged, since magnification (v/u = hi/ho) does not depend on the focal length; the object is still at 2F of the new lens.

marking_points.point: (a) Lens with F1, 2F1, F2, 2F2 marked, object at 2F1
(a) Two correct rays drawn with arrows
(b) Size unchanged (object still at 2F of new lens)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: refraction of different colours, lateral displacement
speed and scattering by colour
questions.question:
Two rays PQ and RS are incident at 35° on a rectangular glass block as shown in the diagram (the two rays are of different colours/wavelengths and bend differently). Observe the diagram and answer the questions that follow.
Which of these two rays will:
(a) have greater lateral displacement on emerging out of the block?
(b) travel with greater speed in the block?
(c) scatter more in the atmosphere?
questions.solution: (a) RS: it bends more towards the normal, so its lateral shift (x2) is greater than that of PQ (x1). (b) PQ: it bends less towards the normal, so it travels faster in the glass. (c) RS: it has the shorter wavelength (PQ has a longer wavelength), so it scatters more.
questions.figure_desc: Rectangular glass block with two rays PQ and RS both incident at 35°; the refracted ray corresponding to RS bends closer to the normal than that of PQ, so the emergent RS ray has the larger lateral shift.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: uses of EM radiations
common property of EM waves
questions.question:
(a) Name the radiations:
1. for which a quartz prism is used to study the spectrum.
2. which are used in remote sensing devices.
3. which are used in traffic signals in India.
(b) Name one property common to all electromagnetic radiations.
questions.solution: (a) 1. Ultraviolet radiation. 2. Infrared radiation. 3. Visible light (red, yellow, green). (b) All electromagnetic radiations travel with the same speed, 3 × 10^8 m/s, in vacuum.

marking_points.point: (b) e.g. same speed in vacuum (3×10^8 m/s) / transverse waves / need no medium

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
concepts: principle of moments with weight of uniform scale at centre
questions.question: Akash takes a uniform metre scale and suspends a weight of 2 N at one end 'X', and a weight of 5 N on the other end 'Y'. He then balances the ruler horizontally on a knife edge placed at 70 cm from X. Draw a diagram of the arrangement and calculate the weight of the ruler.
questions.solution: Diagram: metre scale XY with the knife edge 70 cm from X (30 cm from Y), 2 N hanging at X, 5 N at Y, weight W of the scale acting at its centre (50 cm mark), 20 cm from the pivot on the X side. Clockwise moment (5 N at Y) = 5 × 30 = 150 N cm; anticlockwise moments = 2 × 70 + W × 20 = 140 + 20W. At equilibrium 150 = 140 + 20W, so W = 0.5 N. (Printed solution writes the unit as Nm.)

marking_points.point: Correct diagram with 2 N at X, 5 N at Y, pivot 70 cm from X, scale weight at 50 cm

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: class I lever
mechanical advantage = effort arm / load arm
questions.question:
Three levers X, Y, Z of equal lengths are shown in the diagram.
(a) Which class of lever do these belong to?
(b) Among these (X, Y or Z) which one will give the maximum mechanical advantage? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: (a) Class I levers, since the fulcrum is between the load and the effort. (b) X. MA = effort arm / load arm; for X the effort arm is the greatest compared with its load arm, so it has the maximum mechanical advantage.

marking_points.point: (a) Class I (fulcrum between load and effort)
Justification: MA = effort arm/load arm is largest for X

questions.figure_desc: Three class I levers X, Y, Z of equal length with the fulcrum at different positions; in X the effort arm is longer than the load arm (the fulcrum is nearest the load).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: resonance of sonometer wire
frequency vs mass per unit length
questions.question:
The diagrams given below show two sound boxes A and B with wires of same length (l) and tension (10 kgf) but different cross-sectional areas. Simultaneously, vibrating tuning forks of frequency 300 Hz are placed on the boxes A and B. The paper rider falls off in case of B but not in case of A.
(a) Name and explain the phenomenon responsible for the falling off of the paper rider in B.
(b) The wire A resonates with a tuning fork of frequency 'f'. Is 'f' greater than, less than or equal to 300 Hz? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: (a) Resonance: the natural frequency of the wire in B matches the 300 Hz of the tuning fork, so the wire vibrates with large amplitude and dislodges the paper rider. (b) The thicker wire has greater mass per unit length and hence a lower resonant frequency than a thinner wire (same length, tension, material). So f is less than 300 Hz.

marking_points.point: (a) Explanation: natural frequency of wire = fork frequency, large amplitude vibrations dislodge the rider
(b) Justification linked to mass per unit length / thickness

questions.figure_desc: Two sound boxes A and B each with a stretched wire of length l under 10 kgf tension with a paper rider on the wire; wire cross-sections differ (relative thickness of A and B not stated in the text).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: domestic wiring meter room, main fuse and switch
energy meter unit kWh
questions.question:
The diagram shows wiring in a meter room of a building. X, Y and Z are three devices: X is a fuse, Y is a meter displaying a reading (3528), and Z is a switch.
(a) What is the current rating of device X?
(b) What is the difference between the switch Z shown in the diagram and the switches you use to operate different appliances at home?
(c) What is the unit of the physical quantity displayed in Y?
questions.solution: (a) X is the company (pole) fuse; it has no fixed current rating, it depends on the load capacity of the connection. (b) Z (main switch) connects/disconnects both live and neutral lines simultaneously, whereas household appliance switches connect/disconnect only the live line. (c) kWh (kilowatt-hour).

marking_points.point: (a) Company fuse / no fixed rating, depends on load capacity of connection
(b) Z breaks live and neutral together; appliance switches only the live wire

questions.figure_desc: Meter-room wiring: incoming lines pass through device X (company fuse), an energy meter Y whose display reads 3528, and a main switch Z.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: bulb resistance R = V²/P
series-parallel combination and current
effect of removing parallel branch on brightness
questions.question:
Three identical bulbs B1, B2 and B3 each of power rating 18 W, 12 V are connected to a battery of 12 V. B2 and B3 are in parallel with each other and this combination is in series with B1.
(a) Calculate:
1. the resistance of each bulb
2. the current drawn from the cell
(b) If the bulb B3 is removed from the circuit, then will the brightness of the bulb B1 increase, decrease or remain the same?
questions.solution: (a) 1. P = V²/R: 18 = 144/R, R = 8 Ω. 2. B2 and B3 in parallel = 8×8/(8+8) = 4 Ω; in series with B1: total = 8 + 4 = 12 Ω; current I = V/R = 12/12 = 1 A. (b) With B3 removed, total resistance = 8 + 8 = 16 Ω, current decreases, so the brightness of B1 decreases.

marking_points.point: (a)2 Equivalent resistance 12 Ω (4 Ω parallel + 8 Ω series)
(b) Decreases, with reason (total resistance increases to 16 Ω, current falls)

questions.figure_desc: Circuit with a 12 V battery; bulb B1 in series with the parallel combination of B2 and B3 (arrangement as redrawn in the printed solution).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: calorimetry with latent heat of ice, principle of mixtures
questions.question: 30 g of ice at 0°C is used to bring down the temperature of a certain mass of water at 70°C to 20°C. Find the mass of water [Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 Jg−1°C−1 and specific latent heat of ice = 336 Jg−1.]
questions.solution: Heat gained by ice = 30 × 336 + 30 × 4.2 × 20 = 10080 + 2520 = 12600 J. Heat lost by water = m × 4.2 × 50 = 210 m. Heat gained = heat lost: 12600 = 210 m, m = 60 g.

marking_points.point: Heat to melt ice 30×336 and heat to warm melted ice 30×4.2×20
Heat lost by water m×4.2×50 and equating (calorimetry principle)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: specific heat capacity comparison
calorimeter material needs low specific heat
specific heat changes with state
questions.question:
(a) A certain amount of heat will warm 1 g of material X by 10°C and 1 g of material Y by 40°C. Which material has higher specific heat capacity?
(b) Which material, X or Y, would you select to make a calorimeter?
(c) The specific heat capacity of a substance remains the same when it changes its state from solid to liquid. State True or False.
questions.solution: (a) X: 10 cx = 40 cY, so cx = 4cY. (b) Y, because a calorimeter material should have low specific heat capacity. (c) False; specific heat capacity depends on the phase.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: Fleming's left hand rule, force on current-carrying conductor
effect of cross-section on resistance and current
F = BIL
questions.question:
A copper rod PQ carrying current is kept in a magnetic field between the poles N and S as shown in the diagram (points A and C are marked on either side of the rod).
(a) The copper rod PQ will move towards C. State True or False.
(b) Name the law used to determine the direction of motion of PQ.
(c) What will be the effect on the force experienced, if the rod PQ is replaced by another copper rod of same length but of greater cross-sectional area?
(d) Justify your answer in (c).
questions.solution: (a) True. (b) Fleming's left hand rule. (c) The force increases. (d) Greater cross-sectional area means lower resistance, so more current flows; force F = BIL sinθ increases as I increases.

marking_points.point: (d) Lower resistance gives larger current; F = BIL sinθ

questions.figure_desc: Copper rod PQ across a magnetic field between N and S poles of magnets, current flowing from left to right, field directed downward; points A and C lie on opposite sides of the rod (C is the direction of the force).
